summary: Full brief. I re-measured the transits epoch by epoch, tested the RAVEN row's epochs, refitted triage's difference images with free and fixed-position PRF fits, read TRICERATOPS's scenarios and star list, and checked Gaia DR3, the TIC, WDS, VSX and the quality flags. Nothing kills it: the dip is consistent across 23 PDCSAP transits and the four QLP sectors, the RAVEN row on the star looks like this signal at a 5:2 alias, and the pixels favour the target over the possible hosts 23" and farther. It holds on blending: three Gaia stars 5.2" to 6.8" out that TESS pixels can't separate (NFPP 0.0161), which seeing-limited ground-based photometry would decide; TRICERATOPS had counted one of them twice through a TIC duplicate, which decision 0036 fixed. Updated 2026-10-22 for the 0036 TRICERATOPS rerun.

findings.claim: Three Gaia stars 5.2" to 6.8" from the target could make the dip with 4% to 17% eclipses, TESS pixels can't tell them from the target, and TRICERATOPS's NFPP of 0.0161 sits between its pass and fail bars, so the public data can't say the dip is on the target.

7. Two-star fits. I reran /tmp/t13/heavy.sh uv run python /tmp/t13/399023421-1/two_star.py on jobs_two.json and pairs.json (exit 0; output two_star.out and two_star.json in my folder):
- With 399023424, target SNR is -0.1, 0.3, -1.1, 2.4, 2.0 and the neighbour's is 0.6, 1.1, 1.9, -2.0, -2.1 for S64, S99, S100, S101, S102. That is identical to the finding.
- 993417193 (target 1.7, 2.9, -0.9, -0.1, 0.6; neighbour -1.4, -1.7, 1.2, 0.8, -0.1) and 993417201 (target -0.2, 0.1, -1.0, 2.4, 1.8; neighbour 0.8, 1.3, 1.8, -2.1, -1.8) show the same sign trade.

8. Decision 0036 item 5 and section 3 record the 0.0191 to 0.0161 NFPP move, which is far above the 3e-3 run-to-run noise. The hold's basis, an NFPP between the bars with no blockers, is unchanged.

The rating and the claim match the rules.

1. Rating. The M3 design, section 2 row 5, says of TRICERATOPS: "NFPP > 0.1 fails; anything between is held." Section 4.5 and decision 0026 (Outcomes) give the same bars, and criteria/vet-v3.toml [triceratops] has nfpp_pass 0.001, nfpp_fail 0.1 and fpp_pass 0.5. The draft's triceratops.json has the same sha256 as TRIC3B_RUN's (460576a5...), and its evidence gives outcome inconclusive, nfpp_mean 0.016135 (sd 0.000295), fpp_mean 0.058856, blockers [], missing_hosts [], target ruwe 0.949 and dropped_stars [993417194 DUPLICATE of 399023424]. So the only thing between the signal and a pass is the NFPP, and NFPP sits far from both bars, well outside 0036 item 5's 3e-3 relative noise. Design 4.9 bar 3 and decision 0028 bar 3 require a TRICERATOPS pass, so the signal can't pass. It isn't a fail, so it can't be killed on this either. That is the brief's and 4.9's "held".

2. Deciding evidence. The finding names ground-based photometry, which is on the brief's list and on 4.9's and 0028's. It also says 2-min data would not decide it. That agrees with M3 design 4.5, section 2 row 5, 0026 ("The DDT ask") and 0028 (DDT note): a hold on blending may not go to the DDT ask, because 2-min data use the same 21" pixels.

3. "TESS pixels can't tell them from the target." The three hosts sit 5.2" to 6.8" out (neighbours.csv). That is inside the pixel rule's 15", where 0025 (Context) and 0032 (Decision) say the pixel check can miss a blend (TOI-1399.01). checks.json /pixels passes at 7.9" against 15", so the pixel pass does not clear them.

4. "Nothing in vet-v3 lets cleared neighbours lower the NFPP." This holds. Under 0026 the only outside input is ExoFOP contrast curves. `grep -n "remove_star\|_drop_flagged" src/tess_hunt/tricera.py` shows the only star removal is 0036's drop of DUPLICATE and ARTIFACT rows.

5. "Public data can't decide." The draft's literature.json ExoFOP record has empty files, imaging, comments, tois and ctois, so no public ground-based photometry exists.

6. Host handling follows the rules. All three hosts were weighed, matched to their own TIC stars at 0.008" to 0.016" under Ruling S. Table and TRICERATOPS agree they are possible hosts (design 4.4): required depth 0.168, 0.0956 and 0.0404 against tdepth 0.164, 0.190 and 0.0405. The finding uses the neighbour's RUWE 1.596 as evidence only, not as the target blocker of 0026.

Two imprecisions that don't change the rating:
- "4% to 17%" uses the table's depths. 0025 calls those the least a star could need, and 0026 Ruling M calls TRICERATOPS's tdepth the better-informed number. By TRICERATOPS, 993417201 needs about 19%. The evidence field prints both numbers.
- The list of far stars in the deciding evidence is incomplete. I ran /tmp/t13/399023421-1/addendum-0036/refute-F1-rules/shares.py on the draft probs.csv: last-run NFPP 0.01578. Shares are 399023424 0.00337, 399023447 0.00318, 399023414 0.00295, 993417193 0.00131 and 993417201 0.00112. 399023429 has about 0 (R_s 11.0, a giant). Stars the finding doesn't name hold about 0.0038: 399023401 0.00089, 399023399 0.00079, 399023443 0.00061, 399023427 (11.3") 0.00058, 399023452 0.00049 and smaller ones. The kind of evidence named, seeing-limited photometry on a predicted transit, covers them as well, and the claim never says only those stars matter.

The finding doesn't misread a rule or overstate its evidence, and hold is the rating the design prescribes for an NFPP between the bars.

findings.claim: The RAVEN row on this star (9.825 d, 395 ppm) is most likely this signal at a 5:2 alias, not a second body: the three transits it shares with ours carry no extra depth and neither carry nor make our signal, its other epochs show about half its depth, and RAVEN publishes no row at our period, so our period is not catalogued but the star's dip is, and a CTOI should cite RAVEN.
findings.evidence: Snapshot row ($SNAP3/known.parquet; raw RAVEN/nsfp09_table.csv line 12790): candidate 5, bls_per 9.824768, bls_t0 2345.0358, bls_tdur 3.93 h, bls_depth 394.7 ppm, bls_sde 10.65, bls_mes 1.23, prob_NSFP_mean 0.9975. 9.824768 / 3.926854 (flat fit) = 2.502, and RAVEN's t0 sits at our phase 0.506, so in S37 and S38 its epochs alternate between our transits (182, 187, 192) and our phase 0.5. The paper (Lafarga et al. 2026, MNRAS, arXiv:2603.22597, Zenodo 19661443) searches TESS-SPOC FFIs of S1 to S55, keeps the five highest BLS peaks per star as candidates 1 to 5, and skips only peaks at twice or half a stronger one's period, so a 2.5x alias can survive as peak 5. The star is in neither vet_table.csv nor val_table.csv (downloaded to /tmp/t13/399023421-1/zenodo/; that nsfp09_table.csv has the snapshot's sha256 7b4fb0b02a85...), and nsfp09 holds no other row for it. /tmp/t13/399023421-1/lc_epochs.py (output lc_epochs.txt), on vet-v3's light curve (PDCSAP S11, S37, S38, S64, the checks' detrending, box ephemeris, core half): all 388.2 +- 42.9 ppm (9.06 sigma, equal to checks.json signal_present); without epochs 182, 187, 192 390.1 +- 46.1 (8.47 sigma); those three alone 375.9 +- 116.7; per-epoch depths about their mean chi2 15.0 on 22 dof (p 0.86), epoch 182 -0.87, 187 +1.47, 192 -0.86 sigma; S64, which no RAVEN epoch meets, 420.6 +- 73.9. RAVEN's own ephemeris with our transits masked: 179.9 +- 72.6 ppm over its other epochs (S11 241, 133; S37 170; S38 253; S64 215, 181, -298 ppm); against 116 shifts of its t0 (/tmp/t13/399023421-1/lc_null.py, lc_null.txt) z 3.06, but RAVEN's ephemeris was chosen on S11, S37 and S38, and S64 alone, outside RAVEN's data, gives 148.3 +- 114.0 (1.3 sigma; /tmp/t13/399023421-1/shape_misc.txt), 2.2 sigma short of 395 ppm. A BLS of the residual light curve (our transits masked, lc_null.txt) finds nothing near 9.82 d (SDE 1.74; top peak SDE 4.78 at 13.63 d). Novelty's harmonics (1, 0.5, 2, 1/3, 3) leave out 2.5, so neither novelty nor the 'passed' bar's ExoFOP period match can see such a row.

findings.claim: Nothing points to an eclipsing binary on the target: the depth and U shape rule out a stellar eclipse there, odd and even transits agree, phase 0.5 holds no significant dip, and LEO-Vetter's ModShift secondary at phase 0.435 is not in vet-v3's light curve.

S64's 24 +- 119 rules out an 850 ppm dip every 26.07 d. Ratio 6.64 is no harmonic, and the depth and duration (8 h against our 3.4 h) differ from ours, so it is not the other eclipse of a binary at our period. Whether the two QLP dips are systematics in the timing-suspect sectors or single events on some star was not tested. It decides nothing for 399023421-1.

findings.claim: No artefact makes the signal: no momentum dump falls near a transit, dropping the two transits on raised background moves the depth by at most 15 ppm, no sector dominates, and the per-transit depths agree.
